Gold.note: Central bank buying and rate cut expectations support prices despite extended levels.

Silver.note: Strong solar panel demand and gold beta drive a structural market deficit.

Copper.note: Tight mine supply and grid electrification demand underpin a structural deficit.

Uranium.note: Primary mine supply deficits and restarting global nuclear capacity ensure contract price support.

Lithium.note: Near-term oversupply from new projects offsets slower EV demand growth.

Nickel.note: Surging Indonesian supply continues to overwhelm stainless and battery demand.

Zinc.note: Concentrate shortages and smelter maintenance tighten the refined metal market.

Iron Ore.note: Weak Chinese property sector and high seaborne supply cap upside potential.

Coal.note: High global inventories and peak thermal demand limit long-term price appreciation.

Rare Earths.note: Chinese supply quotas and export restrictions tighten the market for critical magnet metals.

Manganese.note: Steady steel demand is offset by ample South African and Gabonese supply.

PGM.note: Weak auto catalyst demand and metal substitution keep the market well-supplied.

Potash.note: Normalization of global supply chains following recent geopolitical export shocks eases prices.

Aluminum.note: Chinese production capacity caps and rising green energy demand tighten the primary metal market.

Diversified.note: Balanced exposure to copper and iron ore provides a hedge against single-commodity volatility.
